1. PROJECT CONTEXT
Problem definition and project scope
GRIDPULSE  /  PROJECT REVIEW 1
Electricity does not move through one isolated line. A change at one country can change neighbouring flows and the alternatives available during stress.
PREDICTIVE QUESTION
What is likely to happen in the next hour?
Estimate next-hour country net flow from recent history, demand signals, shared network context, and graph centrality.
PRESCRIPTIVE QUESTION
What action can we test when a link is stressed?
Reduce a selected transfer in a scenario, search alternate paths, check headroom and proxy loss, and present the trade-off for human review.
The project scope ends at explainable decision support. It does not control a real transmission grid.

Make the predictive and prescriptive distinction clear. The forecast estimates a future value. The routing module tests a hypothetical intervention and reports consequences. The dashboard recommends; an operator would still need verified engineering constraints.

4. DATA PREPARATION
Preprocessing turns raw files into a safe experiment
GRIDPULSE  /  PROJECT REVIEW 1
Parse
Read both CSV files and convert timestamps to UTC.
Validate
Check missing cells, duplicate keys, country codes, and hourly gaps.
Canonicalize
Map aliases to a stable endpoint pair such as CH-DE.
Align
Join node signals and edge history on the common hourly timeline.
Scale
Fit means and standard deviations only on the training window.
Split
Keep validation and test periods later in time. Do not shuffle across the boundary.
Training-only scaling
x_scaled = (x − μ_train) / σ_train
The same training statistics are applied to validation, test, and live replay inputs.

Source: results/preprocessing_summary.json. Explain why the chronological split matters: using future values while scaling or randomly shuffling would make the evaluation look better than the real forecasting situation.
5. FEATURE DESIGN
Feature extraction keeps the forecast explainable
GRIDPULSE  /  PROJECT REVIEW 1
The experiment uses 11 features per country and hour. They fall into three groups so the model has local evidence, system context, and graph structure.
LOCAL TIME SERIES

Net flow
Actual load
Flow imbalance
Load residual
What is happening at the country now?
NETWORK CONTEXT

Mean net flow across countries
Mean load
Mean imbalance
Mean load residual
What pressure is shared across the system?
STATIC GRAPH

Degree centrality
Closeness centrality
Betweenness centrality
Where does this country sit in the network?
The tensor shape is 12 countries × 960 hours × 11 features. The target is next-hour net flow.

Source: results/feature_catalog.json. Give one simple example: if German load rises while nearby countries also show pressure, the model sees both the local signal and the network context. Centrality does not prove physical causation; it gives the model a stable connectivity descriptor.
6. GRAPH REPRESENTATION
Graph construction and distance-based loss proxy
GRIDPULSE  /  PROJECT REVIEW 1
GRAPH DEFINITION

Nodes represent countries.
Edges represent canonical cross-border interconnectors.
Coordinates support distance and centrality features.
Directional flow history keeps source and target visible.
The graph has 12 nodes and 24 canonical links. The same graph supports forecasting features, stress propagation, resilience ranking, and route search.
LOSS ESTIMATE USED IN SCENARIOS

R = ρL / A

S = |P| / pf

I = S / (√3 V)

P_loss = 3I²R
L comes from the Haversine distance between country-centroid coordinates. The project uses fixed assumptions for voltage, power factor, resistivity, and conductor area.
This is a screening proxy, not an engineering-grade thermal or AC power-flow calculation.

Source: results/dataset_profile.json and the engineering limitations recorded by the pipeline. Explain the purpose of the proxy: compare candidate scenarios consistently. Do not present it as a certified line-loss calculation because actual conductor, route, voltage, and thermal data are missing.
7. FORECASTING SETUP
Model plan and chronological experiment design
GRIDPULSE  /  PROJECT REVIEW 1
BASELINES

Persistence
24-hour moving average
Linear trend
Seasonal naive
These provide reference points before judging the learned models.
FUSION GRU
A recurrent model reads the last 24 hourly steps. It fuses local and global features, then estimates the next-hour net flow.
The checkpoint is trained in PyTorch and loaded by the live API.
DCRNN
A graph recurrent model diffuses information through forward and reverse graph transitions while it processes time.
It tests whether neighbouring countries improve the next-hour forecast.
